title: Shankarashtakam
intro: Lord Shankara is a prominent and benevolent form of Lord Shiva, known as the deity of yoga, transformation, and dissolution.
description:
He Vamadeva Shivashankara Deenabandho Kashipate Pashupate Pashupashanashin ।
He Vishvanatha Bhavabeeja Janartiharin Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥१॥

He Bhaktavatsala Sadashiva He Mahesha He Vishvatata Jagadashraya He Purare ।
Gouripate Mama Pate Mama Prannatha Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥२॥

He Duhkhabhanjaka Vibho Girijesha Shulin He Vedashastravinivedya Janaikabandho ।
He Vyomakesha Bhuvanesha Jagadvishishta Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥३॥

He Dhurjate Girisha He Girijardhadeha He Sarvabhutajanaka Pramathesha Deva ।
He Sarvadevaparipujitapadapadma Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥४॥

He Devadeva Vrishabhadhvaja Nandikesha Kalipate Ganapate Gajacharmavasah ।
He Parvatisha Parameshvara Raksha Shambho Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥५॥

He Virabhadra Bhavavaidya Pinakapane He Neelakantha Madananta Shivakalatra ।
Varanasi-purapate Bhavabhitiharin Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥६॥

He Kalakala Mrida Sharva Sadasahaya He Bhootanatha Bhavabadhaka He Trinetra ।
He Yajnashasaka Yamantaka Yogivandya Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥७॥

He Vedavedya Shashishekhara He Dayalo He Sarvabhutapratipalaka Shulapane ।
He Chandrasurya Shikhinetra Chidekarupa Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha ॥८॥

Shri Shankarashtakamidam Yoganandena Nirmitam ।
Sayam Pratah Pathennityam Sarvapapavinashakam ॥९॥

॥ Iti Shri Yoganandateerthavirachitam Shankarashtakam Sampoornam ॥

faq.a1: It is a sacred devotional hymn dedicated to Lord Shiva, praising His various divine forms, attributes, and cosmic roles.
faq.q2: Who is the author of this hymn?
faq.a2: It was composed by Yogananda Tirtha (श्री योगानन्दतीर्थ).
faq.q3: What is the central prayer of the hymn?
faq.a3: Each of the primary verses concludes with a heartfelt plea to Lord Shiva: "Samsaraduhkhagahanajjagadisha Raksha" — meaning, "O Lord of the Universe, protect me from the dense and impenetrable forest of worldly miseries."
faq.q4: What are the benefits of reciting it?
faq.a4: According to the concluding ninth verse, reciting this Shankarashtakam daily during morning and evening destroys all sins and brings inner peace.
